why:
Doc sentence verified VERBATIM. curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w19.md line 47 (an 'Other wins'
, one sentence, nothing after it that reverses it): 'Hooks now receive the active effort level via the `effort.level` JSON input field and the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable, and Bash tool commands can read \$CLAUDE\_EFFORT' — identical modulo the wrapper and Mintlify backslash escapes in the trailing clause. Independently corroborated on the canonical contract page: hooks.md:635 documents `effort` as a common input field, 'Object with a `level` field holding the active effort level for the turn', 'Present for events that fire within a tool-use context, such as `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `SubagentStop`', and 'The level is also available to hook commands and the Bash tool as the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable.' Repo side verified at the cited lines. `SdkAutomationInput` spans packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742-902; `sed -n '742,902p' | grep -i effort` returns zero hits, so there is no `effort` member of any spelling in the object `hookCommandStdinPayload` (hook-command.ts:641) serialises — it emits `{...input, hook_event_name, cwd?}` and adds nothing. `buildBaseEventEnv` (utils.ts:392) emits NESSY_EVENT/NESSY_EVENT_DATA/NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_SESSION_NAME/NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID/NESSY_SESSION_METADATA plus snake-cased payload mirrors — no effort key. One citation imprecision that does NOT change the consequence: the env builder that actually feeds a command hook is `buildHookCommandEnv` (hook-command.ts:46-81), not `buildBaseEventEnv`; I read it too and it emits NESSY_EVENT, NESSY_EVENT_DATA, six SAFE_INHERITED_ENV_KEYS (HOME/PATH/SHELL/TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP) and fourteen NESSY_* field mirrors, with no effort variable either. So both hook-relevant builders lack it. `grep -rna` (with -a, for the NUL-byte files) over packages/ and apps/ for CLAUDE_EFFORT|NESSY_EFFORT hits exactly three non-test production lines: capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:136 (the SKILL_VARIABLE_SPELLINGS map, `effort: ['NESSY_EFFORT','CLAUDE_EFFORT']`), a comment at :851, and a comment at agent/base-agent.ts:2192 — all describing skill-BODY text substitution (`expandSkillVariables`), which rewrites `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` inside markdown and never sets a process env var. Layer up and layer down both checked. Layer down: the Bash tool runs inside the Pi subprocess, whose env is built at agent/pi-agent.ts:1462-1477 as process.env + proxy vars + envOverrides + AWS + NESSY_SESSION_DIR/NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_DEBUG — no effort variable, so a Bash command cannot read $CLAUDE_EFFORT. Layer up: nothing upstream already supplies it; the value plainly EXISTS and is resolvable at dispatch time (agent/thinking-levels.ts:200 `resolveEffortLevel`, `BaseAgent._thinkingLevel`, consumed at base-agent.ts:2635 and pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:292), and the skill path already consumes exactly this value — so this is an unwired plumbing gap, not a false consequence. Sibling-subsystem check: the identically-spelled `CLAUDE_EFFORT` in runtime-skill-content.ts is the SKILLS subsystem (skills.md:299 `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` body substitution), a different surface from hooks/Bash; the finding names the right subsystem and explicitly disclaims the skills one. Not an owner decision: inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches hook effort. The nearest recorded deviations, in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-effort-precedence.md:177/188/193/197, cover model-config.md's CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL precedence tier and other model-config keys, NOT the hook `effort.level` input field or $CLAUDE_EFFORT on the hook/Bash surfaces. Not a deliberate product difference either: the fork implements effort levels end to end and already ships the Nessy-aliased `${NESSY_EFFORT}`/`${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` skill variable, so this is the same variable simply absent from two other surfaces, not a dropped subscription flow or a rebrand artefact. Only caveat, not load-bearing: under the off-by-default Claude backend the Anthropic Agent SDK may supply its own $CLAUDE_EFFORT to SDK-internal hooks; Nessy's own automations pipeline on the shipped Pi default does not.
correctedState: CONFIRMED with one citation correction. `SdkAutomationInput` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742-902) carries no `effort` member, and `hookCommandStdinPayload` (hook-command.ts:641) serialises that object verbatim, so no hook receives `effort.level`. The env builder that actually feeds a command hook is `buildHookCommandEnv` (hook-command.ts:46-81) — not `buildBaseEventEnv` (utils.ts:392), which serves prompt/webhook automation actions; NEITHER emits an effort variable in either spelling. `CLAUDE_EFFORT`/`NESSY_EFFORT` exist in production only as skill-body text placeholders (runtime-skill-content.ts:136), never as a process env var, and the Pi subprocess env (pi-agent.ts:1462-1477) omits them, so a Bash command cannot read one either. The value itself is available — `resolveEffortLevel` (thinking-levels.ts:200) over `BaseAgent._thinkingLevel`, already consumed by the skill path at base-agent.ts:2635 — so the gap is unwired plumbing on the hook and Bash surfaces, not a missing feature.
